features: THE FIELDS THAT ASKED FOR WHAT THEY DID NOT NEED — One migration: the database is touched. It makes three previously mandatory columns optional: a unit's description, its internal number, and a document's description. No data is modified — whoever already has a description keeps it, whoever has an internal number keeps it. This version comes from four reports by one administrator on the forum, all filed the same day and all about the same screen.

«DESCRIPTION (OPTIONAL)», AND THEN IT WAS MANDATORY. The label said so and the program did not: uploading a document for a unit, leaving the description empty produced an error. Two texts written at different times that nobody had compared — the edit screen, in fact, already declared it optional. The same when creating a unit: description mandatory for no reason, with a column that accepted empty at database level and no calculation reading it.

THE INTERNAL NUMBER, AND THE PARKING SPACE THAT HAS NONE. «For an external parking space not linked to a flat I don't think it makes sense to enter this»: the observation was right, and the internal number is now optional. There was a consequence the report could not foresee: in ten places of the program the internal number was the only way the unit was named. The worst was the PDF statement of account — the document handed to the owner — where a unit without one appeared as «Int. » and nothing else.

NOW EVERY PLACE FALLS BACK ON THE UNIT'S NAME, which stays mandatory — which is why the fallback always exists. When registering a payment, where the search filtered on the internal number, you can now search by name too.

THE 4 MB FILE REFUSED ON A SCREEN THAT ANNOUNCED 10. Three numbers were in play, and the winner was always the one we did not declare: the screen said 10 MB, the check accepted 20, and the reporter's server stopped at 2. When a file exceeds PHP's limit it never reaches the program, and all that was left was «upload failed», which gave no way to understand where the problem was. Now there is a single limit, read from the server, and both screens of a unit's document state that one (the program's other six upload points still carry the fixed number: they go into 1.10.1).

TWO LIMITS, TWO DIFFERENT MESSAGES. Exceeding the single-file limit gives an error under the field; exceeding the whole-request one used to produce an «expired session» page, and now says the file is too large. And when the upload fails for other reasons — full disk, temporary folder not writable — the message no longer tells you to shrink a file that is perfectly fine.

THE OFFICIAL DOCKER IMAGES WERE THE WORST CASE: none declared a limit, so nginx's default applied — 1 MB. Anyone installing with our image could not upload even a 1.5 MB PDF while the screen promised 20. All three images now carry the same values, consistent with each other.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE A CONTAINER REBUILD. Docker users can now ask the program whether uploaded documents are safe, with «php artisan kondomanager:verifica-persistenza». It answers with how many files and how many megabytes are at stake, and if the folder lives inside the container — where it would vanish on the next recreation — it explains where to declare the volume.

THE REST. In a unit's and a supplier's menu two entries stayed highlighted at once, because the first one's address is a prefix of all the others. And when a write fails, the error message now carries a six-character reference that can be found in the server log: «it doesn't work» becomes «it doesn't work, ref. 4F2A1C».
